title: Microwave-Induced Optomagnetism in High-Temperature Superconductors
authors: Anoop Dhillon, Amir Borji, Hamed Majedi
abstract: We report the first experimental observation of a steady-state, microwave-driven inverse Faraday effect in a high-temperature superconductor. Circularly polarized microwave radiation generates a helicity-dependent response in an epitaxial $\mathrm{YBa_2Cu_3O_{7-δ}}$ film, detected using homodyne Hall transport. The optomagnetic response emerges exclusively below $T_c$, vanishes in the normal state, and exhibits no power-dependent counterpart under linearly polarized excitation. The effective optomagnetic conversion reaches $1.75\,\mathrm{T}/(\mathrm{W\,cm^{-2}})$, surpassing optical benchmarks by several orders of magnitude. At higher microwave powers, the signal collapses when the self-generated field exceeds $B_{c1}$, marking the onset of a vortex phase-slip regime, and subsequently re-emerges at mode-locked vortex-washboard harmonics. These results establish steady-state microwave optomagnetism as a route to contactless, non-inductive magnetic control and nonequilibrium vortex spectroscopy in superconducting quantum systems.
summary: This work reports the first experimental detection of microwave-induced optomagnetism in YBCO superconductors. By measuring the helicity-dependent Hall voltage, the authors demonstrate that the response is governed by the superconducting state and undergoes dramatic changes as the applied field induces vortex motion. This establishes a novel, contactless method for studying vortex dynamics and magnetic control in superconducting quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper reports the first experimental observation of a steady-state, microwave-driven Inverse Faraday Effect (IFE) in a high-temperature superconductor.
main_result: The optomagnetic response is robustly observed below the critical temperature, showing a distinct collapse above the lower critical field ($B_{c1}$) and re-emerging at harmonics corresponding to mode-locked vortex motion.
method: The experiment uses a low-noise homodyne transport apparatus to measure the helicity-dependent Hall voltage response to circularly polarized microwave radiation.
model_or_system: The system is an epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7-delta film, a high-temperature superconductor. The analysis combines a two-fluid model for the superconducting condensate and normal electrons with mesoscopic vortex dynamics.
key_observables: Helicity-dependent Hall voltage ($	ilde{V}_H$), power-dependent signal magnitude, and the alignment of signal re-emergence with vortex washboard harmonics.
important_parameters: Temperature relative to $T_c$, microwave power, and the lower critical field ($B_{c1}$).
main_assumptions: The measurement assumes the Hall voltage can isolate the intrinsic optomagnetic response from parasitic effects, and that the low-power signal is dominated by the intrinsic IFE.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the power dependence of the signal, showing the Meissner state, the collapse above $B_{c1}$, and the subsequent re-emergence of peaks aligned with predicted vortex washboard harmonics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework (IFE in HTS) to presenting the experimental setup and measurements, detailing the distinct regimes: low-field Meissner state, vortex entry/collapse, and finally, the coherent re-emergence of the signal at high powers.
why_interesting: The study provides a non-dissipative, microwave-driven method to probe non-equilibrium vortex dynamics and magnetic control in superconductors, which is highly relevant for understanding superconducting quantum devices.
